title: Armor of God, Fruit of the Spirit, Gifts of the Spirit
description: A Back to the Bible study comparing three essential aspects of the Christian life — standing firm, growing in character, and serving others.
author: ROLCC Fellowship Team

sections.heading: Observe
sections.body: Scripture describes three distinct but connected realities in the believer's life. Ephesians 6 calls us to put on the whole armor of God — the belt of truth, breastplate of righteousness, shoes of the gospel of peace, shield of faith, helmet of salvation, and sword of the Spirit. Galatians 5 lists the fruit of the Spirit: love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness, and self-control. First Corinthians 12 describes gifts of the Spirit given to each believer for the profit of all — including wisdom, knowledge, faith, healing, miracles, prophecy, discernment, tongues, and interpretation.

sections.heading: Interpret
sections.body: Each area serves a different purpose. The armor protects — its function is to help us stand against the enemy (Ephesians 6:11). The fruit produces — its purpose is to make us like Christ in character. The gifts empower — they are given so we can serve others and build up the body of Christ. Armor answers "How do I stand?" Fruit answers "Who am I becoming?" Gifts answer "How can I serve?" Many Christians focus on one area while neglecting the others, but God desires believers who are protected, transformed, and empowered.

sections.heading: Apply
sections.body: Picture a soldier: armor is his equipment — without it he is vulnerable. Fruit is his character — without it he is unstable. Gifts are his abilities and assignments — without them he is ineffective. Armor protects him. Fruit shapes him. Gifts use him. A mature believer needs all three. Which area do you focus on most? Which do you tend to neglect? Spiritual gifts without spiritual maturity can leave us effective in ministry but weak in character.

discussionQuestions: Which of the three areas — armor, fruit, or gifts — do you focus on most?
Which area do you tend to neglect?
Can someone have spiritual gifts without spiritual maturity?
How do the armor, fruit, and gifts work together in the life of a believer?

quiz.question: What is the main purpose of the armor of God?
quiz.explanation: Ephesians 6:11 calls believers to stand firm.

quiz.question: What is the fruit of the Spirit meant to produce?
Why are spiritual gifts given according to 1 Corinthians 12:7?
quiz.explanation: Gifts are for building up the body of Christ.

quiz.question: In the soldier analogy, what does the fruit of the Spirit represent?
quiz.explanation: Fruit shapes who the believer is becoming.

quiz.question: What is a sign of spiritual maturity in this study?
options: Focusing on only one of the three areas
quiz.explanation: God desires believers with armor, fruit, and gifts together.
